title: The Content Paradox: Why Making AI Writing Easier Makes the Internet Worse

comments.author: ryan
comments.text:
## Editorial pass 2026-08-29

Shipped 2026-08-28. No copywriting work here. Two notes so it stays useful on the board.

**Its remaining value is as a link target.** The Jevons argument — cheaper generation explodes volume, not quality — is upstream of several unshipped stories, and it is the natural thing to point at rather than re-argue. It is currently missing from 37add6's links list. Worth a sweep across in-flight stories for the same omission.

**Board hygiene.** Sits at `idea`, which reads as "not started" and is the opposite of true. Same permanent mismatch as Bugonomics: reaching `published` would mean walking every gate and writing every artifact. Fine to leave parked, but do not let it read as an open pitch.

**One editorial note if it is ever revised:** this piece and 8bde91 (Never Use Fast) are arguing adjacent economics from opposite ends — one about the cost of generation collapsing, one about spending the savings well. If a third economics piece ever gets pitched, check it is not a third telling of the same Jevons argument.
